title: oncall-snippet-curator-and-failure-anchoring
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: on-call responders repeatedly paste long logs and ad-hoc commands into ticket threads. This PR introduces a compact "snippet curator" that extracts minimal reproduction snippets (command lines, essential logs, sanitized traces) and pairs them with a small "failure anchor": a telemetry fingerprint (span id + metric delta) that points back to the most relevant time window in observability systems. The intent is to reduce triage time, improve reproducibility, and provide a small, shareable artifact that incident-bots and playbooks can reference.

What this change does: a) adds a curator pipeline in the incident-bot that detects candidate snippets from incident messages and attachments, b) applies deterministic sanitizers to remove secrets and PII, c) synthesizes a one-line reproduction command or diagnostic (when possible), and d) computes a failure-anchor token (service:span:metricDelta@timestamp) that maps to our telemetry index to speed-nav to the root cause window.

Key features: - Heuristic snippet extraction (logs, stack frames, curl/pg commands) - Sanitization layers (K/V redaction, IP anonymization, key pattern removal) - Compact curated artifact (metadata + snippet + anchor) that can be embedded in playbooks and runbooks - /curate CLI and bot slash-command to request a curated artifact - JSON schema compatibility with slo-toolkit snapshot importer for later analysis

Release checklist: - [x] Unit tests for sanitizers and anchors - [x] Integration test with synthetic incident payloads - [x] CI lint/format passes - [x] Manual smoke test against staging telemetry index - [x] Docs: playbook section and example snippets in docs/oncall-curation.md

Backward compatibility: curated artifacts are optional attachments; existing workflows that expect raw messages are unchanged. The curator stores artifacts to the incident attachments blob store and emits a small metadata event to the event bus.

Security notes: sanitization is conservative by default; any detected secret-like token is replaced with <REDACTED>. We intentionally do not execute extracted commands; the one-line reproduction suggestion is non-executable (annotated) and clearly marked. Customers can opt-out via the incident-bot config flag 'curation.enabled=false'.

How to test locally: run `./scripts/dev-bot --playback testdata/sampled-incident.json --enable-curation` and POST a message with an example curl/psql snippet. The curated artifact will appear under the /attachments API and the failure-anchor token will be included in the event payload.

Notes on the failure-anchor: anchors are deterministic hashes over (service, span_signature, metric_name, minute_bucket) with a stable prefix to allow quick lookups from observability. We include a TTL hint for index retention and a confidence score computed from pattern matches.

Related Linear: ENG-6812, ENG-6843. Related PRs: will follow with a small slo-toolkit importer to consume the curated artifacts for retrospective analyses.

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Overall nice work — sanitizer behavior looks good. Please add an explicit test covering IPv6 redaction (we've had issues with earlier regexes).
Nora Alvarez: Can the failure-anchor include a sampling hint? If the metric we anchor to is low-volume the anchor can be noisy. Suggest adding confidence bucket metadata.
Maya Chen: replied: added ipv6 test and a 'confidence_bucket' field in the artifact metadata (low/medium/high) computed from pattern counts).
Samir Gupta: approved after minor doc tweak request.
CI Bot: all checks passed (unit, integration, lint).
release_notes: Add oncall snippet curator that produces sanitized, compact reproduction snippets and failure-anchor tokens for quicker triage; configurable and opt-outtable.
